title: Prompting and Retrieval
tagline: In-context learning, prompt design, structured output, embeddings, vector search and retrieval-augmented generation
summary: Much of what a language model can do is unlocked by what you put in its context. This course covers in-context learning and prompt design, structured output, text embeddings and vector search, retrieval-augmented generation and its evaluation, and the problem of hallucination.

chapters.title: In-context learning
chapters.summary: Zero- and few-shot prompting, and theories of why in-context learning works.

chapters.title: Prompt design
chapters.summary: Instructions, examples, roles and formatting, and systematic prompt engineering.

chapters.title: Structured output
chapters.summary: JSON and schema-constrained generation, grammars and parsing model output.

chapters.title: Text embeddings
chapters.summary: Sentence embeddings, contrastive training and similarity search.

chapters.title: Vector search
chapters.summary: Nearest-neighbour search, approximate indexes such as HNSW, and hybrid keyword and vector search.

chapters.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
chapters.summary: Chunking, retrieval, reranking and grounding answers in sources.

chapters.title: Hallucination and grounding
chapters.summary: Why models state falsehoods, citations, abstention and calibration.

chapters.title: Evaluating retrieval systems
chapters.summary: Retrieval metrics, answer faithfulness and end-to-end evaluation.
